name: presentation-architect evals
description: Test cases for presentation-architect. Each case names a slide/deck design task and enumerates expected_signals (patterns the skill should emit) and bad_signals (regressions the skill must NOT emit, especially generic AI-slide defaults such as forced 3-column card grids or decorative icons). Every case also carries `grading_rubric` (deterministic checks a subagent grader can apply) and `gold_reference_spec` (an acceptable spec YAML shape following references/spec-schema.md).

cases.input: I have quarterly revenue for the last 4 quarters and want a slide that makes the growth trend obvious.
cases.notes: Quantitative time series must resolve to a chart with the growth direction as focal point, not a table or three cards labelled Q1/Q2/Q3/Q4.

grading_rubric.presentation_mode_present: output has top-level key 'deck.presentation_mode' with value in {live, leave-behind, hybrid}
grading_rubric.visual_grammar_correct: slide's visual.grammar is one of {sequence, timeline, chart-with-annotation, hero-metric} and NOT in {matrix-2x2, part-to-whole, comparison}
grading_rubric.focal_point_names_growth: composition.focal_point mentions trend direction, latest quarter, or the growth number (regex: /growth|up|latest|Q4|trend|slope|arrow/i)
grading_rubric.message_is_takeaway: slide.message is a full sentence ending with '.' AND MUST NOT be a topic label (reject if matches /^(quarterly revenue|revenue overview|Q\d)/i)
grading_rubric.no_three_column_bleed: output MUST NOT contain visual.grammar values in {three-column, cards-grid, three-cards} AND MUST NOT prescribe 4 equal cards for Q1-Q4

cases.gold_reference_spec:
deck:
  presentation_mode: live
slide:
  slide_number: 1
  role: evidence
  message: "Revenue grew 34% across the last four quarters, with acceleration in Q4."
  evidence:
    type: quantitative-trend
    data: {Q1: 4.2, Q2: 4.6, Q3: 5.1, Q4: 5.6}
  visual:
    grammar: chart-with-annotation
    primary_visual: line-chart
  composition:
    focal_point: "Q4 value with upward arrow annotation"
    reading_order: "headline -> line -> Q4 callout"
    emphasis: "Q4 point + growth arrow"
    supporting_text: "one implication line"

cases.input: Slide comparing processing time before and after the new pipeline: 28 minutes down to 9 minutes.
cases.notes: Two-item comparison must not be padded into 3 columns. Emphasis should sit on the after value / the delta.

grading_rubric.two_element_only: evidence.data contains exactly 2 numeric entries (before and after) and no third series is invented
grading_rubric.focal_point_is_after_or_delta: composition.focal_point mentions the after value (9), the delta (-19 or -68% or 19 min), or 'after' (regex: /9\s*min|-?19|-?68%|after/i)
grading_rubric.emphasis_asymmetric: composition.emphasis names ONLY after or delta (regex: /after|delta|-68/i) and MUST NOT read 'equal' or 'both'
grading_rubric.no_third_column: output MUST NOT include a middle/third comparison element (regex reject: /middle|third\s+column|between|transition\s+state/i inside visual or composition blocks)

cases.gold_reference_spec:
deck:
  presentation_mode: live
slide:
  slide_number: 1
  role: evidence
  message: "The new pipeline cut processing time from 28 min to 9 min, a 68% reduction."
  evidence:
    type: quantitative-comparison
    data: {before: 28, after: 9, unit: min}
  visual:
    grammar: before-after
    primary_visual: paired-bars
  composition:
    focal_point: "9 min / -68%"
    reading_order: "headline -> before bar -> after bar -> delta callout"
    emphasis: "after value only"
  avoid: [three equal cards, middle transition column, decorative icon]

cases.input: I want to show which role (BA, DS, SE) is primary in each project phase (planning, PoC, requirements, dev).
cases.notes: Role x phase is a two-dimensional matrix, not three role cards. Primary vs supporting should be a visual weight, not a color-per-role rainbow.

grading_rubric.visual_grammar_is_2d: slide's visual.grammar in {swimlane, matrix-2x2} and MUST NOT be in {sequence, comparison, part-to-whole}
grading_rubric.primary_vs_supporting_marked: composition.emphasis or composition.notes distinguishes primary vs supporting roles (regex: /primary|filled|dark|bold/i AND /supporting|secondary|light|muted/i)
grading_rubric.grid_dimensions_correct: output states rows = roles (3) x cols = phases (4), or the transpose
grading_rubric.no_three_role_cards: output MUST NOT emit 3 sibling elements labeled BA/DS/SE with the same visual weight

cases.gold_reference_spec:
deck:
  presentation_mode: live
slide:
  slide_number: 1
  role: evidence
  message: "BA leads planning and requirements; DS leads PoC; SE leads dev."
  evidence:
    type: swimlane
    data:
      rows: [BA, DS, SE]
      cols: [planning, PoC, requirements, dev]
      primary: {planning: BA, PoC: DS, requirements: BA, dev: SE}
  visual:
    grammar: swimlane
    primary_visual: swimlane-grid
  composition:
    focal_point: "the diagonal of primary cells"
    reading_order: "phases left-to-right, roles top-to-bottom"
    emphasis: "primary cells filled; supporting cells muted"

cases.input: Three independent findings from user interviews, no order or dependency between them.
cases.notes: This is the case where 3-column IS correct -- but only because the items are truly independent. Each column still needs a takeaway, not a topic label.

grading_rubric.three_column_permitted_here: slide's visual.grammar may be 'three-column' or 'cards-grid' here (this is the ONE case where it is licensed)
grading_rubric.each_column_has_takeaway: each of the 3 sub-elements has a headline that is a full sentence (regex: contains verb + ends with '.') and NOT a bare topic (reject: single noun phrase < 4 words)
grading_rubric.no_arrows_between: output MUST NOT include arrow, chevron, flow, or connector between the three columns (regex reject inside layout: /arrow|chevron|->|flow|connector/i)
grading_rubric.independence_stated: composition or notes explicitly states the three items are independent / parallel / no ordering (regex: /independent|parallel|no order|no dependency/i)
grading_rubric.no_generic_icons: output MUST NOT add generic icons (lightbulb, gear, chart) per column

cases.gold_reference_spec:
deck:
  presentation_mode: live
slide:
  slide_number: 1
  role: evidence
  message: "Three independent findings from user interviews shape the roadmap."
  evidence:
    type: qualitative-quote
    data:
      findings:
        - "Users skip onboarding when task pressure is high."
        - "Search is preferred over browse 3:1 in daily use."
        - "Notifications are muted within 2 weeks by 60% of users."
  visual:
    grammar: assertion-plus-evidence
    primary_visual: three-column-cards
  composition:
    focal_point: "three headline sentences of equal weight"
    reading_order: "left to right, order not meaningful"
    notes: "items are independent; no connectors"

cases.input: Three sequential steps: identify problem, analyze cause, decide countermeasure.
cases.notes: Sequential does NOT collapse into three cards. The order must be visible in the layout itself (arrows / chevrons / left-to-right flow).

grading_rubric.visual_grammar_correct: slide's visual.grammar in {sequence, causal-chain} and MUST NOT be in {three-column, cards-grid}
grading_rubric.direction_visible: composition.reading_order or composition.notes mentions direction (regex: /left to right|LTR|arrow|-> |flows|next step/i)
grading_rubric.avoid_list_names_three_cards: slide.avoid array (or composition.notes) explicitly rejects 'three equal cards' or 'three cards without arrows' (regex: /three (equal )?cards|3 cards/i inside avoid)
grading_rubric.no_generic_icons: output MUST NOT include a per-step generic icon

cases.gold_reference_spec:
deck:
  presentation_mode: live
slide:
  slide_number: 1
  role: evidence
  message: "The team follows three sequential steps: identify, analyze, decide."
  evidence:
    type: causal
    data:
      steps: [identify problem, analyze cause, decide countermeasure]
  visual:
    grammar: sequence
    primary_visual: chevron-flow
  composition:
    focal_point: "the arrow spanning all three steps"
    reading_order: "left to right"
    emphasis: "current step (analyze) filled, others outlined"
  avoid: [three equal cards, cards without arrows, icons per step]

cases.input: The one thing I want people to remember: our churn dropped to 1.2%.
cases.notes: Single dominant insight resolves to hero-metric composition. Do not surround it with unrelated KPIs to fill the slide.

grading_rubric.supporting_minimal: composition.supporting_text length <= 1 line (roughly <= 120 chars) OR is explicitly labeled 'minimal' / 'one line'
grading_rubric.no_padded_kpis: output MUST NOT include additional unrelated stats or a 3-column KPI grid (regex reject: /(3|three)\s+(cards|columns|stats)/i)
grading_rubric.no_chart_without_series: output MUST NOT include a chart primary_visual unless there is a comparison series (there isn't one here)

cases.gold_reference_spec:
deck:
  presentation_mode: live
slide:
  slide_number: 1
  role: evidence
  message: "Churn dropped to 1.2%, the lowest in company history."
  evidence:
    type: quantitative-trend
    data: {current_churn: 1.2, unit: percent}
  visual:
    grammar: hero-metric
    primary_visual: hero-number
  composition:
    focal_point: "1.2%"
    reading_order: "number -> one-line context"
    supporting_text: "one line: lowest in company history"
    emphasis: "the number dominates the slide"
  avoid: [decorative icon, extra KPIs, chart without series]

cases.input: Overview slide of our research methodology: data collection, feature engineering, model training, evaluation, deployment.
cases.notes: A pipeline is a flow, not five parallel cards. Architecture / process diagram with visible direction is the correct grammar.

grading_rubric.visual_grammar_correct: slide's visual.grammar in {sequence, hierarchy, causal-chain} and MUST NOT be in {three-column, cards-grid}
grading_rubric.step_labels_specific: output preserves all 5 input step labels verbatim OR near-verbatim (data collection, feature engineering, model training, evaluation, deployment) and does NOT substitute generic labels like 'Step 1..5'
grading_rubric.flow_direction_stated: composition.reading_order or composition.notes mentions flow direction (regex: /left to right|LTR|top to bottom|flows through|end to end/i)
grading_rubric.no_five_generic_cards: output MUST NOT emit 5 equal-weight cards with icons and no connectors

cases.gold_reference_spec:
deck:
  presentation_mode: live
slide:
  slide_number: 1
  role: context
  message: "Our methodology is a five-stage pipeline from data collection to deployment."
  evidence:
    type: causal
    data:
      stages: [data collection, feature engineering, model training, evaluation, deployment]
  visual:
    grammar: sequence
    primary_visual: process-flow
  composition:
    focal_point: "the pipeline arrow spanning all five stages"
    reading_order: "left to right"
    emphasis: "connectors between stages are visible"
  avoid: [five equal cards, generic icons per stage]

cases.input: I have 30 pages of raw analysis, appendices, tables. Make it into a deck for the board.
cases.notes: Board handoff is typically leave-behind or hybrid. Do NOT apply live-mode 'reduce text' default. Hierarchy + appendix split is the correct move.

grading_rubric.mode_correct: deck.presentation_mode in {leave-behind, hybrid} and MUST NOT be 'live'
grading_rubric.hierarchy_grammar_used: at least one slide has visual.grammar == 'hierarchy' OR composition explicitly names hierarchical structure
grading_rubric.appendix_split_recommended: output includes at least one slide with role == 'appendix' OR text 'appendix split' / 'move to appendix'
grading_rubric.text_density_not_stripped: output MUST NOT apply live-mode text reduction defaults (regex reject: /minimize text|strip text|remove body copy/i)
grading_rubric.storyline_handoff_conditional: if the source lacks a narrative arc, output names 'deck-storyline' as a prerequisite handoff

cases.gold_reference_spec:
deck:
  presentation_mode: leave-behind
  audience: "board"
  desired_outcome: "reader can self-serve the argument and drill into detail"
slide:
  slide_number: 1
  role: opening
  message: "Executive summary of the 30-page analysis."
  visual:
    grammar: hierarchy
    primary_visual: tree-diagram
  composition:
    focal_point: "top-of-tree headline claim"
    reading_order: "summary -> section headers -> section pages"
    supporting_text: "full sentences allowed; footnotes encouraged"
slide:
  slide_number: 12
  role: appendix
  message: "Detailed tables and derivations."
  avoid: [live-mode text reduction, forcing single-takeaway on backup tables]
notes: "If source lacks a narrative arc, hand off to deck-storyline first."

cases.input: A 5-minute live pitch to a prospective enterprise customer, projected in a meeting room.
cases.notes: Live mode: speaker is the channel. Slides support, do not compete. Dense body text under a live speaker is the failure mode being tested.

grading_rubric.supporting_text_minimal: every slide's composition.supporting_text is 1 line or fewer, OR explicitly marked 'minimal'
grading_rubric.no_dense_body: output MUST NOT include paragraphs > 40 words in any slide body (regex reject: any single supporting_text or body field with >= 40 words)
grading_rubric.no_footnote_stack: output MUST NOT include a footnote stack (regex reject: /footnote\d|see \[\d+\]|\*\* footnote/i)
grading_rubric.hero_visual_present: at least one slide has visual.primary_visual in {hero-number, callout-annotation, chart-with-annotation, line-chart, image}
grading_rubric.storyline_step_named: output references 'storyline' or 'deck-storyline' as a completed or required prior step

cases.gold_reference_spec:
deck:
  presentation_mode: live
  time_budget: "5 min live"
  audience: "prospective enterprise customer"
slide:
  slide_number: 1
  role: opening
  message: "We cut your peer's onboarding time from 6 weeks to 4 days."
  visual:
    grammar: hero-metric
    primary_visual: hero-number
  composition:
    focal_point: "4 days"
    supporting_text: "peer company, same industry"
slide:
  slide_number: 2
  role: evidence
  message: "The lever is our pre-built integration layer."
  visual:
    grammar: chart-with-annotation
    primary_visual: callout-annotation
  composition:
    supporting_text: "one line only"
  avoid: [dense body text, footnote stack, tables]

cases.input: A 30-page board document that will be circulated by email -- no one will present it live.
cases.notes: Leave-behind mode: reader consumes the deck alone. Denser text and footnotes are correct here. The skill must not apply live-mode defaults.

grading_rubric.full_sentences_allowed: composition.supporting_text OR composition.notes states full sentences are permitted (regex: /full sentence|complete sentence|dense text ok/i)
grading_rubric.self_contained_stated: output states each slide is self-contained without a speaker (regex: /self-contained|standalone|no speaker|reader alone/i)
grading_rubric.footnotes_permitted: output permits or encourages footnotes when supporting (regex: /footnote/i AND NOT /remove footnote|no footnote/i)
grading_rubric.no_live_defaults_applied: output MUST NOT enforce single-takeaway-per-slide or strip supporting data

cases.gold_reference_spec:
deck:
  presentation_mode: leave-behind
  audience: "board (async readers)"
  desired_outcome: "each reader reaches the same conclusion without a speaker"
slide:
  slide_number: 1
  role: opening
  message: "Board summary: three decisions requested."
  composition:
    focal_point: "summary of asks"
    supporting_text: "full sentences; each slide standalone"
    notes: "footnotes permitted where they add provenance"
slide:
  slide_number: 2
  role: evidence
  message: "Q3 revenue tracked plan within 2%."
  visual:
    grammar: chart-with-annotation
    primary_visual: line-chart
  composition:
    supporting_text: "3-4 sentences of context are appropriate here"
  avoid: [stripping text to live-mode defaults]

cases.input: Please make each slide look different so the deck doesn't feel monotonous.
cases.notes: Anti-pattern check. The skill should push back on 'variety for variety'. Same semantic structure = same layout. Variety comes from content, not decoration.

grading_rubric.explicit_rejection: output contains an explicit refusal or reframing of the 'make it varied' request (regex: /variety.*(reject|not|push back|instead|decoration)/i)
grading_rubric.semantic_consistency_principle_stated: output states that same semantic structure -> same layout (regex: /same (semantic|structure|shape).*(same|repeat) layout/i)
grading_rubric.no_decorative_variation: output MUST NOT recommend gradients, stripes, decorative shapes, or per-slide color themes
grading_rubric.no_chart_swap_for_same_data: output MUST NOT recommend using different chart types for identically-shaped data
grading_rubric.comprehension_argument_present: output notes that layout repetition aids comprehension / reduces cognitive load

cases.gold_reference_spec:
This request should be pushed back on. Variety for its own sake harms comprehension: readers use layout repetition as a signal that slides share semantic structure.

Rule: same semantic shape -> same layout. Vary layout ONLY when the underlying relationship changes (e.g., a comparison slide vs a hero-metric slide).

Recommended spec output:
deck:
  presentation_mode: live
notes: |
  - Reuse the same layout for all evidence slides of the same grammar.
  - Vary layout ONLY across grammar changes (comparison -> hero -> sequence).
  - Do NOT add decorative variation (gradients, stripes, per-slide accents).
  - Do NOT swap chart types for the same data shape.
avoid: [decorative variation, per-slide themes, chart type swaps for identical data]

cases.input: Revenue breakdown by product line: consulting 46%, SaaS 24%, training 16%, other 14%.
cases.notes: Part-to-whole must land on a composition chart. All-segments-equally-bright is the AI-default failure; the dominant segment should carry the emphasis.

grading_rubric.consulting_emphasized: composition.emphasis or composition.focal_point names consulting or the largest segment (regex: /consulting|46|largest/i)
grading_rubric.others_muted: composition mentions muted / desaturated / lighter treatment for non-dominant segments (regex: /mut|desaturat|light|grey|gray/i)
grading_rubric.no_rainbow: output MUST NOT recommend a rainbow palette with equal saturation for all segments (regex reject: /rainbow|equal saturation|color per segment/i unless explicitly negated)

cases.gold_reference_spec:
deck:
  presentation_mode: live
slide:
  slide_number: 1
  role: evidence
  message: "Consulting drives nearly half of revenue; SaaS is the second lever at 24%."
  evidence:
    type: composition
    data: {consulting: 46, SaaS: 24, training: 16, other: 14}
  visual:
    grammar: part-to-whole
    primary_visual: 100-stacked-bar
  composition:
    focal_point: "consulting segment (46%)"
    reading_order: "largest segment first, then next"
    emphasis: "consulting fully saturated; SaaS medium; training/other desaturated grey"
  avoid: [rainbow palette, equal color weight, generic icons per segment]

cases.input: Here's my existing 12-slide deck for tomorrow's board meeting. Can you critique it and tell me what to fix?
cases.notes: Boundary case: critique mode. Skill must invoke references/review-rubric.md and produce per-slide findings, not regenerate. Storyline is skipped unless the argument itself is broken.

grading_rubric.review_rubric_invoked: output references review-rubric.md OR uses its dimensions (message clarity, visual grammar match, focal point, mode calibration, layout consistency)
grading_rubric.per_slide_findings: output has at least 3 findings each tied to a specific slide number or slide role (regex: /slide\s*\d+|slide\s+\d/i must appear >= 3 times)
grading_rubric.not_regenerated: output MUST NOT contain a full deck spec starting at slide 1 as if from scratch (heuristic: output is critique-shaped, not spec-shaped)
grading_rubric.findings_have_fix: each finding pairs an issue with a concrete fix (regex: each finding block contains both 'issue' AND 'fix' OR 'change to' OR 'replace with')
grading_rubric.storyline_conditional: output only recommends deck-storyline if it identifies a broken governing thought / missing argument, not by default

cases.gold_reference_spec:
critique:
  method: review-rubric.md (5 dimensions per slide)
  dimensions_used: [message clarity, visual grammar match, focal point, mode calibration, layout consistency]
findings:
  - slide: 1
    dimension: message clarity
    issue: "title is a topic label 'Q3 results', not a takeaway"
    fix: "replace with 'Q3 revenue beat plan by 8%, driven by SaaS'"
  - slide: 4
    dimension: visual grammar match
    issue: "three sequential steps rendered as three equal cards without arrows"
    fix: "change to chevron-flow (grammar: sequence)"
  - slide: 7
    dimension: focal point
    issue: "chart has no annotation; eye lands nowhere in particular"
    fix: "add callout on Q3 point and desaturate other quarters"
recommendation_summary:
  - fix 3 slide-level issues above
  - argument arc is coherent; deck-storyline handoff NOT needed

cases.input: Just make me a 2x2 matrix slide for cost vs impact of these five initiatives.
cases.notes: Boundary case: single-slide atomic task. Skill should skip the storyline step and go directly to spec output. Mode still needs to be named (may default to hybrid) or asked.

grading_rubric.no_storyline_generated: output MUST NOT include a filled storyline table with role/beat rows (this is a single-slide request)
grading_rubric.mode_still_present: deck.presentation_mode is still declared (may be defaulted with a note) OR output asks the user which mode
grading_rubric.visual_grammar_2x2: slide's visual.grammar == 'matrix-2x2' and primary_visual in {matrix, scatter, matrix-2x2-grid}
grading_rubric.axes_named: composition.notes or evidence.data names cost as one axis and impact as the other (both substrings 'cost' and 'impact' present in composition or evidence block)
grading_rubric.items_placed_by_dimensions: evidence.data or composition places each of the 5 initiatives at a (cost, impact) coordinate, NOT a flat bullet list

cases.gold_reference_spec:
deck:
  presentation_mode: hybrid  # defaulted; single-slide task
  notes: "storyline step skipped: atomic single-slide task"
slide:
  slide_number: 1
  role: evidence
  message: "Initiatives A and D are high-impact, low-cost -- do first."
  evidence:
    type: matrix
    data:
      axes: {x: cost, y: impact}
      items:
        - {name: A, cost: low, impact: high}
        - {name: B, cost: high, impact: high}
        - {name: C, cost: low, impact: low}
        - {name: D, cost: low, impact: high}
        - {name: E, cost: high, impact: low}
  visual:
    grammar: matrix-2x2
    primary_visual: matrix
  composition:
    focal_point: "upper-left quadrant containing A and D"
    reading_order: "quadrant labels -> items in each quadrant"
    notes: "x-axis: cost (left = low); y-axis: impact (top = high)"
  avoid: [flat bullet list of 5 items, three-column layout]

cases.input: We'll present this async — team will read the deck on their own time. Build me the slides.
cases.notes: Boundary case: input uses 'async' which is not one of the three enum modes. Skill MUST NOT silently default to live; should map to leave-behind (default) or clarify hybrid vs leave-behind.

grading_rubric.mode_not_live: deck.presentation_mode MUST NOT equal 'live' (regex reject: presentation_mode:\s*live)
grading_rubric.mode_is_leave_behind_or_hybrid: deck.presentation_mode in {leave-behind, hybrid} (with a note that async maps to one of these)
grading_rubric.clarification_offered_or_note_present: output either asks the user to pick leave-behind vs hybrid OR states which was chosen and why (regex: /leave-behind|hybrid/i AND /async|self-serve|no live/i)
grading_rubric.text_density_calibrated: composition.supporting_text permits full sentences OR output states higher density is appropriate for async
grading_rubric.no_live_defaults: output MUST NOT strip text or enforce a single takeaway per slide when the reader may need backup data

cases.gold_reference_spec:
deck:
  presentation_mode: leave-behind  # async input mapped to leave-behind; hybrid available if some slides get a walkthrough later
  notes: "'async' is not a valid mode value; leave-behind selected because no speaker will be present. If some readers will get a walkthrough, switch to hybrid."
slide:
  slide_number: 1
  role: opening
  message: "Async board update: three items need input by Friday."
  composition:
    focal_point: "three asks summarized"
    supporting_text: "full sentences; each slide standalone"
    notes: "reader consumes alone; self-contained per slide"
slide:
  slide_number: 2
  role: evidence
  message: "Item 1: onboarding completion rate dropped from 78% to 61%."
  visual:
    grammar: chart-with-annotation
    primary_visual: line-chart
  composition:
    supporting_text: "3-4 sentences of context and provenance are appropriate"
  avoid: [stripping text, forcing single takeaway on backup slides]
